title: Lost platform
brief: Build a small original audio drama package for two performers, about a station platform that appears on an obsolete timetable. The performance is for a community radio slot of about three minutes and must work without a narrator or licensed music. Deliver something the performers and producer can rehearse and stage; the story, production choices and file organization are yours.

files.name: Top Pocket.html
files.body:
Top Pocket

Script · 1 / 3

Q1 · First punch. Let it ring for two seconds.

VALThat is a ticket punch. You put it through a ticket. You have just put a hole through Thursday.
KITIt was folded up under the short leg of the bench. Look what it says under my thumb.
VALPlatform Half. Oh, give me that.
KITHalf of what?
VALHalf a minute. That was as long as they could get the mail train to stand. Look at the date on it, Kit. I was twelve.
KITWell, somebody ought to tell the wall.
VALTell the wall what?

Q2 · Masonry slides. Give it the full five seconds.

KITThat it can come back now.
VALThere used to be a blue gate there. My dad had to lift me up to see over it.
KITI can see over it. There’s a little trolley. There’s a sack on it.
VALGet your fingers out of that latch.
KITVal. The label’s got your handwriting.

Hold two beats.

Turn after “handwriting.”

Top Pocket

Script · 2 / 3
VALI know. I used to do the labels. Dad said mine was the only writing the postman could read in the rain.
KITYou sent a whole sack to yourself?
VALRead the little box. That’s the sender.
KITThen where was it going?
VALNowhere. They took the stop off the timetable. Everybody came down anyway. Mrs Bell brought a cake with a train on it. We put all the letters in the sack and Dad shut the gate.
KITWhat happened to the cake?
VALWe ate it. What do you think we did?

Q3 · A bell winds down. Wait for its last tap.

VALOh. That used to mean fifteen seconds.
KITTake this end.
VALYou’ll tear it. Get your arms under it. Under, like a baby.
KITWhat sort of baby have you been carrying?
VALLeave the trolley!

Q2 · Wall moves back. Both haul together on one breath. Let the scrape finish.

KITAll right. You can put the baby down.
Turn as the sack lands.

Top Pocket

Script · 3 / 3
VALThere must be two hundred letters here. Half these houses will be shops.
KITHere’s one we can deliver.
VALThat one hasn’t even got a stamp.
KITIt says “Dad, top pocket.” I think that’s enough of an address.
VALHe made me put it in the sack. Said if I wanted to work the mail I had to trust it.
KITDo you want me to turn round?
VALStay there. May I borrow your top pocket? His coat had the same little flap. Lift it for me.

Four seconds. KIT lifts the flap. VAL slips the envelope into the pocket.

VALThere. That’s one.
KITHow do we do the others?
VALMrs Bell’s girl still cuts my hair. She’ll know who moved where. Turn Thursday over. We’ll need a list.
KITAnd what’s going to hold the bench up?
VALYour foot. Till we finish.

Q1 · Final punch. Hold two seconds, then out.

End.

Top Pocket

Producer’s sheet

Two voices · mono · target 3:00 from first punch to silence. Print the first three pages for each performer.

At the microphones

Val works the station. She can still see exactly where her father’s coat pocket was. Kit, her younger workmate, has been sent to fix a rocking bench. Kit has found a punch and a timetable. Start halfway through their shift, with the mild irritation of two people who like each other.

Keep both voices close. At the gate, have Kit look past Val’s shoulder while staying on mic. After the haul, let both catch their breath through their next lines. At “Stay there,” Kit goes still enough for Val to deliver the letter. Let the small delivery take its four seconds.

Sound cart

Load the three included mono WAVs as one-shots. Start each on the script’s italic cue. Keep the wall behind the breath on its return. The two silent holds need no room effect. All five triggers run in order below.

1. Q1 · punch before the first word. A hard clack and spring return.

2. Q2 · wall after “Tell the wall what?” Five seconds, ending in a stone settling.

3. Q3 · bell after “What do you think we did?” A small mechanical bell runs out of turns.

4. Replay Q2 after “Leave the trolley!” Same movement in reverse story direction.

5. Replay Q1 after “Till we finish.” Kit punches the list. Count two seconds from the strike and close both mics.

Clock rehearsal

Start a stopwatch on Q1. The script has about 390 spoken words. Start around 150 words per minute. Aim to reach “handwriting” near 1:00 and put the sack down near 2:00. Play the cake exchange lightly and pick up the hauling lines on each other’s breath. If the read runs long, tighten the early exchanges so the pocket scene can keep its silence.

For live foley, snap a hole punch for Q1, drag a rough block along a board for Q2 and tap a mug with a spoon in a slowing roll for Q3. Have the producer handle all three.

files.name: 01 - Performance script.md
files.body:
# Where the Tide Stops

An audio drama for two performers. Target running time 3:00.

- **MARA** brings an old timetable and a tobacco tin. Her father can no longer get down to the shore.
- **IVO** used to work this station. He still has the hand lamp he used on the platform.

*Only names in bold introduce spoken lines. Times are rehearsal marks. Sound in brackets is cued by the producer.*

### 0:00–0:27

*[A. A large sheet of paper unfolds, close.]*

**IVO**  
You could have brought that in the morning.

**MARA**  
It says eleven fifty-eight. I thought we ought to be here when it says.

**IVO**  
Where did you find it?

**MARA**  
Behind Dad’s kitchen clock. See the thumbtack holes?

**IVO**  
I put those there. We pinned it to the booking-office door thirty years ago.

### 0:27–0:55

**MARA**  
What’s the little four beside the time?

**IVO**  
Platform four.

**MARA**  
There are only three.

**IVO**  
Four was down those steps. You could feel the boards lift when the tide came in. We filled the steps with concrete when they built the sea wall.

**MARA**  
Dad says he used to take his boots off down there. The nurse thought he meant the bath.

*[Give Ivo a beat to take that in.]*

### 0:55–1:21

**IVO**  
What’s in the tin?

**MARA**  
Nothing yet. I thought there might be a stone left. He taught me to listen for the little ones rolling back down the beach.

**IVO**  
Let me see the bottom of that.

*[B. Paper turns.]*

**MARA**  
“Request stop. Show a white light.”

**IVO**  
The lamp still works.

*[C. A switch clicks. A beat.]*

### 1:21–1:51

*[D. A low rail hum swells and gives way to water rolling over shingle. Listen for the first wash before Ivo speaks.]*

**IVO**  
Get back. That’s the edge.

**MARA**  
That was solid concrete.

**IVO**  
There’s one under your foot now. Hold my sleeve.

**MARA**  
Is there a train?

**IVO**  
I don’t see one. Keep hold.

*[The wash recedes. Mara takes in what’s within reach.]*

**MARA**  
There. Just where the water went out.

### 1:51–2:18

*[E. The tin opens. Two small pebbles tap inside.]*

**IVO**  
You got one?

**MARA**  
Two. The other’s flat. Wait. Hold the light lower.

*[F. A small scoop of water into the tin. The lid presses shut.]*

**IVO**  
Up you come. Have you got the rail?

**MARA**  
I’ve got you.

*[A breath as they steady themselves.]*

**IVO**  
Ready?

**MARA**  
Yes. Put it out.

*[G. The switch clicks off. Leave a beat of quiet.]*

### 2:18–2:44

**IVO**  
Concrete again.

**MARA**  
Here. Cup your hands. Keep it level.

*[H. The tin changes hands. A small tilt makes pebble and water move together.]*

**IVO**  
He used to make me take my boots off, too. Said I’d never hear a thing with them on.

**MARA**  
Did you?

**IVO**  
Once. I left my socks on. He laughed all the way back up the steps.

### 2:44–3:00

**MARA**  
Come round in the morning. Tell him that bit.

*[Allow a beat for Ivo’s answer.]*

**IVO**  
All right. You carry the tin. My hands are shaking.

*[I. A final small wash inside the tin. Let it settle into room tone. End at 3:00.]*

files.name: 02 - Producer sheet.md
files.body:
# Where the Tide Stops · Producer sheet

Run time **3:00** from the paper opening to the end of the room-tone tail. Play the two parts close to the mic. The piece uses voices, Foley and one mono sound cue. There is no music.

Open [the performance script](01%20-%20Performance%20script.md) for both performers. Load [Tide at platform four](03%20-%20Tide%20at%20platform%20four.wav) onto one playback pad or track. It plays once from **1:21 to 1:47**. The other sounds can be made at a Foley station or recorded individually with the same props.

## Set up

- Give Mara a folded sheet and a shallow metal tin with a snug lid, two small clean pebbles and a spoonful of water in a cup. During the handoff, tilt the closed tin just enough to move the water and one pebble. Try it over a towel first.
- Use a clicky hand lamp or a mechanical switch for Ivo. With one mic, keep both actors at a consistent distance and angle the Foley across the mic so the tin taps stay below speech.
- Start with a few seconds of clean studio room tone on hand for the edit. In a live run, leave the voice mics open through the quiet beats.

## Call the cues

Times are checkpoints. Use the line or action to follow the cast. Cue D is the main timing anchor.

| Cue | Target | Trigger and sound |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | 0:00 | On the start signal, unfold the paper in one clear movement. Ivo comes in as it settles. |
| B | 1:08 | After Ivo asks to see the bottom, turn the sheet. Mara reads the instruction. |
| C | 1:19 | After “The lamp still works,” click the switch on. Give the click its own space. |
| D | 1:21 | Start the tide file after the click. Let the low rumble turn into the first wash, about six seconds into the file, before Ivo says “Get back.” Ride the cue down under the voices. Let the second wash recede by Mara’s “There.” The file tails out on its own. |
| E | 1:51 | After “Just where the water went out,” open the tin and let the two pebbles tap inside. |
| F | 2:00 | After “Hold the light lower,” tip a small spoonful of water into the tin and seat the lid. |
| G | 2:16 | After “Yes. Put it out,” click the switch off. Hold the quiet until Ivo speaks. |
| H | 2:24 | After “Keep it level,” pass the tin and tilt it once. Give Ivo a moment to hear it. |
| I | 2:55 | After “My hands are shaking,” take back the tin and tilt it again. Let the tiny wash settle and carry the room tone to 3:00. |

For live Foley in place of D, rub a felt pad slowly along a metal tray for the opening rail sound. Bring up a slow back-and-forth wash in a shallow pan of water and clean gravel, starting about six seconds after the rail sound begins. Make a second, smaller wash about 16 seconds in. Ease to quiet by 1:47. Keep the tin at a separate mic position or bring it closer so its first taps read as a new sound.

## Rehearse to the slot

Run the opening exchange and the platform history through 0:55 as a flow of questions and answers. Leave time for the sound before Ivo’s warning and for both performers to hear the tin at the end. Ivo’s first warning is instinctive. Mara listens for the pebbles before reaching for them. Play the last exchange as an ordinary invitation.

On a stopwatch pass, aim to land the last line by 2:55. If the read runs long, tighten the early conversational gaps first. If it runs short, give the washes and handoff more time. Keep the final tin movement audible before the cut.
